components.css: .ds-set-card { overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--border, #d3dcef); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--panel, #fff); color: var(--fg, #101d3a); font: 500 14px/1.45 system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-set-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; min-height: 60px; padding: 12px 16px; } .ds-set-row + .ds-set-row { border-top: 1px solid var(--border, #d3dcef); } .ds-set-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; } .ds-set-text span, .ds-set-value { color: var(--muted, #51607f); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 400; } .ds-set-value { flex-shrink: 0; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-switch { appearance: none; flex-shrink: 0; width: 38px; height: 22px; margin: 0; padding: 2px; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg, #101d3a) 26%, transparent); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-switch::before { content: ''; display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--primary-fg, #fff); transition: translate 0.15s; } .ds-switch:checked { background: var(--primary, #145cff); } .ds-switch:checked::before { translate: 16px; } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus, #145cff); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The extension appears for a moment, hands over the right key and steps aside. Nothing in it competes with the page the user came from: surfaces are plain navy or plain paper, type is the system's own, and one electric-blue button per screen says where the way through is. Everything else is an outline, a row or a line of text.

Components are calm and certain. Corners are moderately rounded, nothing casts a shadow at rest, and state changes in 120ms. The density is that of a tool that is opened fifty times a day: rows of 36 to 40 pixels, labels at 12 and 13, and room only where a screen has a single thing to ask (sign in, unlock).

It follows the browser's light or dark scheme and has no theme switch. Both themes are the same system: the same roles, the same steps between surfaces.

Rejected, by decision: decorative gradients and glass or blur effects; illustrations, mascots and emoji; any brand colour beyond the three it has.
keyCharacteristics: Three brand colours, used by role: navy grounds, blue acts, cyan points.
Depth by tone (background, sheet, card), not by shadow.
One filled button per screen; the rest are outlined or text.
System fonts only; monospace only for secrets.
Line icons at one stroke, drawn inline.
Every motion is short, eased out, and has a reduced-motion rule beside it.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: A screen has one filled Electric Blue button: the way through it. A second action is outlined; a way out is text.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: A component names a role (`--card`, `--muted`), never a hex. A new surface picks from the existing steps before a step is added.

rules.name: The Edge Rule
rules.body: Something to type in is outlined with `field-border`, not `border`. Dividers may be faint; a field's edge may not.

rules.name: The No Fourth Colour Rule
rules.body: Navy, blue and cyan are the brand. Status colours are status only and never decorate.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Anything that counts or dates (list counts, the version, stats, "last used") sets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Secrets Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks a value that is copied character by character: passwords and code in notes. It is not a style.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: Centred headings and notes use `text-wrap: balance`, so no line ends in an orphan.

rules.name: The Room Is Kept Rule
rules.body: A control that appears on hover (a row's actions) keeps its space while hidden, so text beside it never jumps.

rules.name: The Truncate, Don't Wrap Rule
rules.body: Names, addresses and emails in rows are one line with an ellipsis; only notes and errors wrap.

rules.name: The Flat At Rest Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is over the page and temporary". Cards, sheets and buttons never have one.

rules.name: The Functional Effect Rule
rules.body: The only blur is the veil over a hidden secure note, and the only gradient is the fade under a sticky form footer. Both hide content on purpose; neither is decoration, and no other use is added.

dos: Do give each screen exactly one filled Electric Blue button.
Do build depth from the three tones (background, sheet, card) and a 1px divider.
Do use the semantic tokens, and check a new pairing in both themes.
Do outline anything typed into with `field-border` (3:1), and show its focus on the box.
Do pair every transition and animation with a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule, and keep state changes at 120ms ease-out.
Do keep a hidden control's room, and truncate one-line text with an ellipsis.
Do use `tabular-nums` for counts and dates, and monospace for secrets.
Do draw new icons inline on the 24 grid with a 2px round stroke.
donts: Don't add decorative gradients, glass, backdrop blur or glows. Surfaces are plain.
Don't add illustrations, mascots or emoji. The mark and the line icons are the only pictures.
Don't introduce a brand colour beyond navy, blue and cyan, or use a status colour as decoration.
Don't put a shadow on anything that is not floating over the page.
Don't nest a card in a card, or thicken a border for emphasis.
Don't load a remote font, icon set, script or stylesheet: extension pages run under a CSP that allows only their own files.
Don't write a raw hex in a component.
Don't put a spinner in a button; change its label.
